title: Deep Contextualized Word Representations
summary: Matthew E. Peters, Mark Neumann, Mohit Iyyer, Matt Gardner, Christopher Clark, Kenton Lee, and Luke Zettlemoyer submitted 'Deep contextualized word representations' on February 15, 2018, introducing deep contextualized word representations learned as functions of the internal states of a pretrained deep bidirectional language model.
significance: A documented natural-language-processing research milestone for contextual word representation, demonstrating representations that vary with linguistic context and can be added to downstream models across multiple NLP tasks.

verification.note: The original arXiv record establishes the February 15, 2018 first-submission date, authors, and the introduction of deep contextualized word representations learned from internal states of a pretrained deep bidirectional language model. The ACL Anthology independently corroborates the paper, authors, 2018 NAACL publication context, and technical abstract. This record uses the arXiv submission date strictly as a research-publication milestone. It does not infer an exact software-release date, geography, institutional affiliation, ancestry, influence, causality, or relationships.
